solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for softly

indicators.note: a dangerous thing is wild and unstable, so the letters of abyss are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A walker gives a perilous chasm a wide berth, stepping quietly around it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' reads as clothing but is the verb meaning go round; 'dangerous' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To skirt something is to go round its edge without entering, which is what passing by does.

clue.text: Europeans grabbing microphone for controversy and debate

indicators.note: the Europeans grab hold of the microphone, so the one word is held inside the other

parts.note: Poles are natives of Poland, so Europeans
mic is the short form of microphone

explanation.surface: Continental delegates seize the microphone in a heated argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemics is the practice of fierce argument, a heated dispute carried on in speech or print.

clue.text: Perhaps Arabian ecofreak's description of incorruptibility

parts.note: the Arabian is one example of a sea
an ecofreak is a green, an environmental campaigner

explanation.surface: An Arab environmental zealot is somehow being described as beyond bribery.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlyle called Robespierre 'the sea-green Incorruptible', so the colour phrase became a byword for a man who cannot be bought.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: Robespierre was famously labelled with this colour as the Incorruptible, making it a literary epithet for unbribable virtue.

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central pair of letters of the word are cut out

parts.note: belles are beautiful women, the sort pictured as pin-ups

explanation.surface: Gatherings of glamour models who have no feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: A bee is a social gathering for shared work or contest, as in a spelling or sewing bee.

clue.text: User of police in a poll

indicators.note: the police force is placed in among the words a poll, sitting between them

parts.note: the poll is an old word for the head
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Someone who makes use of the police appears in an opinion survey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'User' looks innocent but is a drug user; 'poll' is not a vote but the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug user who takes LSD habitually is called this, so 'user' in the narcotics sense fits.

clue.text: Firm talking about loud noise leads to working in harmony

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: the speechmaking goes round the noise, enclosing it

parts.note: orating is making speeches, so talking
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A company making a racket in its speeches somehow ends up with everyone pulling together.
explanation.definitionFit: To coordinate is to bring parts into an efficient, harmonious working relationship.

indicators.note: the American sits in Denmark, inside its abbreviation

parts.note: DK is the international code for Denmark
US, the United States, stands for American

explanation.surface: An American visitor in Denmark watches the evening fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is the time of twilight when daylight fades and night is coming on.

parts.note: looks like a farewell, but read as two byes, cricket runs scored without the batsman hitting the ball, which are counted among the sundries

explanation.surface: A cheery goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run conceded when the ball passes the batsman untouched; such runs are lumped together as sundries, so two of them are plural sundries.
explanation.definitionFit: Byes are one kind of sundry run in cricket, so more than one bye are sundries of that name.

clue.text: Take car first: one could be artful

indicators.note: the car comes first, placed before the other piece

parts.note: Dodge is an American make of car
R (recipe) is the abbreviation for take, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Instructions to grab a vehicle before anything else, from someone sly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Artful Dodger is the young pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: Dickens's pickpocket is called the Artful one, so an evasive trickster could be an artful one.

indicators.note: the greeting is placed among the letters of the French article, inside it

parts.note: les is French for 'the' (plural)
ave is a Latin word of greeting, hail or welcome

explanation.surface: Someone leaving is greeted warmly by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who goes away from a place goes, sets off, as verbs in the third person.

clue.text: Mollycoddled female student in second group? On the contrary

indicators.note: the surface puts the student in the group, which is then turned round
this reverses the relation, so it is the group that goes inside the female student

parts.note: a coed is a female student at a mixed college
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A pampered young woman placed in a second set at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' alone would put the student inside the group; 'On the contrary' flips it so the group goes inside the student.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone pampered and overprotected has been fussed over and treated indulgently.

clue.text: Having revolting habits means lushes need hosing to be reformed

indicators.note: reformed means re-shaped, so the letters of the two words are made anew in another order

explanation.surface: Drunks with disgusting ways need hosing down if they are going to change.
explanation.definitionFit: Being morbid and repellent in one's tastes, delighting in the macabre, is what having revolting habits describes.

indicators.note: heard signals the word is taken for how it sounds, not its spelling

parts.note: to mourn is to grieve

explanation.surface: Someone is told to do their weeping before the midday meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The poetic word for morning, the part of the day before noon and its meal.

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged differently from how they stand

explanation.surface: Perhaps the hair dye goes on everybody's heads.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade is a particular tone or variety of a colour, like a hue.

indicators.note: the word is drawn out of the letters of deceased, part of it

explanation.surface: A solemn phrase for the remains, or the repose, of the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest of the deceased' reads like 'rest in peace', but 'of' picks letters out of 'deceased'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: relaxation and relief from effort, a state of repose.

parts.note: doctor the word who and it becomes how, so a 'doctored who' is what produces the clue word

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how anyone could journey through time.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who, the BBC science-fiction hero, travels through time in the TARDIS; read his name as an instruction, 'doctor WHO', and it rearranges into 'how'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of the long-running BBC series is a Time Lord who travels through history.

parts.note: an ass is a donkey
ay (or aye) is an old word meaning always, ever

explanation.surface: A donkey persistently has a go at something.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic sense of the noun is an attempt or endeavour, besides its sense of a test of metal.

parts.note: reads as a comment on Noel Coward's play Blithe Spirit, but means the condition of being in a blithe, happy spirit

explanation.surface: A review of how Noel Coward's comedy is faring.
explanation.walkthrough: Blithe Spirit is a Noel Coward comedy; capital letters hide that 'blithe spirit' simply means a happy mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means happy and carefree, so the condition of a blithe spirit is gladness and good humour.

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
to solve is to find the answer

explanation.surface: A sailor works out the truth and pardons the offender.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to release someone from guilt or blame is to pardon them.

clue.text: Neat fish is beginning to eat sulphur and becomes rusty

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

indicators.note: the fish starts to eat the word is, taking it inside itself

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Cattle and fish start eating sulphur and corrode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is not tidy but the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Rust is iron oxide, so metal turning rusty is combining with oxygen.

parts.note: looks like an instruction to turn up later, but means a gift due in December

explanation.surface: A note asking someone to attend in a few weeks' time.
explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas box is a British term for a tip or gift given at Christmas to tradespeople such as the postman.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasonal gratuity handed over in December, the month after this one if read in November.

clue.text: Putting it in scruffy furs could produce consequences

indicators.note: it is put in among the jumbled letters of furs
scruffy means untidy and unkempt, so furs is jumbled

explanation.surface: Stuffing something into a shabby fur coat might lead to trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scruffy' gives FRUS, the rearranged letters of the coat material, before 'in' sets the pronoun inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Results or outcomes of actions are their fruits, as in reaping the benefit of labour.

clue.text: Fighting with little time for passion

parts.note: war is fighting
mth is a short form of month, a little stretch of time

explanation.surface: Brief combat followed by a moment of ardour.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: warmth of feeling is ardour, intensity of emotion.

definitions.meaning: the back end, a bottom or hindquarters
as a horse does when it lifts onto its hind legs

explanation.surface: A tail lifted high.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is the back part or behind; as a verb it means lift up or stand on hind legs.

parts.note: shin is a letter of the Hebrew alphabet
E, as in é, is taken as a French letter here; the clue word letters covers both

explanation.surface: A list of a Polish, a Hebrew and a French alphabet, or else correspondence in three languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb meaning buff up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to buff something until it gleams is to polish it.

clue.text: This could be indicative of temper

definitions.meaning: the indicative is a grammatical ... of verbs, alongside subjunctive and imperative
a frame of mind or humour, as in being in a bad temper

explanation.surface: A hint that someone's bad humour shows.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the indicative is one such verb category; in feeling, a temper is a passing state of mind.

clue.text: Sport adds up to nothing: not special

indicators.note: not says the abbreviation for special is left out of the rest

parts.note: sums means adds up
O, the figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A sporting result that comes to zero, nothing special.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Japanese heavyweight wrestling is a national sport.

parts.note: the daw, or jackdaw, is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird sings to welcome a fresh day.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is the start of the morning, so the two are used interchangeably.

clue.text: I'm on public transport and feet

parts.note: I'm expanded is I am
buses are public transport

explanation.surface: A commuter announces they are on the bus and on foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feet' are metrical feet in poetry, not the ones you walk on.
explanation.definitionFit: An iamb is a metrical foot of an unstressed then stressed syllable, so these are poetic feet.

clue.text: Dispenses with one in expressions of farewell

indicators.note: one goes in, inside the gestures of goodbye

parts.note: waves of the hand say goodbye
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone does without one of the goodbyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to forgo a right or requirement is to set it aside, do without it.

parts.note: the elk is called a moose in North America

explanation.surface: A large deer in the classroom causes everyone to chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to chat in a friendly, ingratiating way, chit-chat.

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters of noises are set in another order

explanation.surface: A trade union is told to stop its noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like a command to stop but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek term for political union, used for the Greek Cypriot campaign to join Cyprus to Greece.
